description: A constraint_violations entry may optionally back-reference the grader_results entry that detected it via grader_id, for the common case where the violation was produced by a scored dimension rather than being independent of any grader -- raised by @MSKazemi (MSKazemi/aobench#51) using AOBench's own shape as the motivating example: the RBAC hard fail is produced by the governance grader, which is ALSO one of the seven independently-scored dimensions (0.20 weight in default_hpc_v01). Without a back-reference, a consumer cannot tell whether the failing 'governance' grader_results entry and the 'rbac_scope' constraint_violations entry describe one event or two, which double-counts a single breach in any human-facing summary (e.g. rendering both 'failed the governance grader AND violated an authorization constraint' for what is actually one breach). grader_id is optional and purely additive -- this fixture is schema-valid with or without it; it exists to pin the cross-reference shape once producers start using it.
